examples.text: Everyone felt **relaxed** at the beach.

right.label: ✓ For people and calm times
right.text: I feel **relaxed** after a hot shower.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for the thing that calms you
wrong.text: The massage was so relaxed.

meaning: Wanting very much to do something.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The kids are **eager** to open their gifts.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: He's **eager** to show us his new bike.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for something you hate
wrong.text: I'm eager to visit the dentist; I hate it.

meaning: Serious and sad.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The house was **sombre** after the funeral.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: His voice turned **sombre** when he spoke of his father.

right.label: ✓ For serious, sad moods
right.text: It was a **sombre** day for the family.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for parties
wrong.text: The birthday party was loud and sombre.

check.question: Which word fits the mood at a funeral?

meaning: Pleased because you got what you wanted.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: I'm **satisfied** with how the room looks.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: Are you **satisfied** with your new phone?

wrong.label: ✗ Not "satisfied from"
wrong.text: I'm satisfied from the food.

meaning: To fear something that is going to happen.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: I **dread** Monday mornings.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: She used to **dread** speaking in class.

wrong.label: ✗ Not "dread of" as a verb
wrong.text: I dread of exams.

meaning: Very surprised and upset.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: We were **shocked** by the electricity bill.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: I was **shocked** to hear they broke up.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for the shocking thing
wrong.text: The news was very shocked.

options.text: I was shocked by the news.

meaning: Accepting something bad because you can't change it.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Dad is **resigned** to the long drive every day.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: She sounded **resigned** about missing the trip.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for fighting back
wrong.text: She was resigned, so she argued all night.

meaning: Truly sorry for something wrong you did.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: My son was **contrite** after breaking the window.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: He sent a **contrite** message after the fight.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for laughing off a mistake
wrong.text: He was contrite and laughed about the mess he made.

meaning: Happy and moved by someone's kindness.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: I was **touched** that my kids made me breakfast.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: She was **touched** by your card.

wrong.label: ✗ Not "touching" for the feeling
wrong.text: I am very touching by your gift.

check.question: Your neighbour brings soup when you're ill. You feel…

meaning: A bit embarrassed because you made a small mistake.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: He gave a **sheepish** smile after burning the toast.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: She looked **sheepish** when she arrived an hour late.

right.label: ✓ For small, silly mistakes
right.text: I felt **sheepish** about forgetting her name.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for showing off
wrong.text: He was sheepish and boasted about it.

meaning: Very, very sad, often after a loss.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The kids were **heartbroken** when the puppy died.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: He was **heartbroken** after the break-up.

right.label: ✓ For a deep loss or love ending
right.text: She was **heartbroken** to leave her home.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for small letdowns
wrong.text: I'm heartbroken my coffee is cold.

meaning: Too pleased with yourself, in an annoying way.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: My brother looked **smug** after winning the board game.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: Don't be so **smug** just because you were right.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for kind, humble pride
wrong.text: She felt smug and thanked everyone who helped.

options.text: He looked smug after winning and kept bragging.

meaning: Shocked and upset by bad news.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: We were **dismayed** to find the fridge had stopped working.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: She was **dismayed** by how much the city had changed.

right.label: ✓ Dismayed by or to
right.text: He was **dismayed** to see the mess.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for good news
wrong.text: I was dismayed to win the trip.

meaning: Worried and tense because of too much to deal with.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: I'm **stressed** about the move.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: He gets **stressed** when the house is full of guests.

wrong.label: ✗ Not "stressful" for the person
wrong.text: I am so stressful today.

meaning: Silly and excited; also a little dizzy.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The kids were **giddy** on the last day of school.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: We felt **giddy** after the good news.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for deep sadness
wrong.text: He was giddy with grief at the funeral.

check.question: Kids bounce around on the last day of school. Which word fits?

meaning: Very pleased.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Grandma was **delighted** with the flowers.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: I'm **delighted** you could make it.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for the thing that pleases
wrong.text: The meal was delighted.

meaning: Nervous and confused because you're rushed.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: I got **flustered** when the guests arrived early.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: She gets **flustered** when people stare.

right.label: ✓ When rushed or watched
right.text: He got **flustered** and forgot his lines.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for calm, clear thinking
wrong.text: She stayed flustered and solved it calmly.

meaning: So pleased with how things are that you stop trying.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Don't get **complacent** just because the garden looks good.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: We got **complacent** after winning and lost the next match.

right.label: ✓ For relaxing too much after success

wrong.label: ✗ Not the same as "content"
wrong.text: I'm complacent with my simple, happy life.

options.text: We got complacent and stopped practising.

meaning: Sad because something wasn't as good as you hoped.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Dad was **disappointed** with my marks.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: I'm **disappointed** the concert was cancelled.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for the thing that lets you down
wrong.text: The film was very disappointed.

meaning: Shaken and nervous after something upsetting.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The loud thunder left the kids **rattled**.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: He got **rattled** when they changed the plan at the last minute.

right.label: ✓ After a shock or pressure
right.text: She was **rattled** by the angry call.

wrong.label: ✗ Not with "cool" or "steady"
wrong.text: He stayed rattled and cool all game.

meaning: Not able to wait calmly.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: The kids are **impatient** for dinner.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: Don't be **impatient**; she's almost here.

right.label: ✓ Impatient with a person, for a thing

wrong.label: ✗ Not "unpatient"
wrong.text: I'm very unpatient.

options.text: She gets impatient in long queues.

meaning: Making you feel happy and full of kindness.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: It was **heartwarming** to see Grandpa play with the baby.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: Her speech was so **heartwarming**.

right.label: ✓ For the thing, not the person

wrong.label: ✗ Not for the person who feels it
wrong.text: I am heartwarming after the story.

rule: for the moment, not the person

meaning: A little sorry about something, often with a small smile.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: He gave a **rueful** laugh about the burnt rice.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: She was **rueful** about missing the early-bird offer.

wrong.label: ✗ Not for real anger
wrong.text: She was rueful and slammed the door.

meaning: Wanting to know or learn about something.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: My daughter is **curious** about how planes fly.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: I'm **curious** to see his new flat.

wrong.label: ✗ Not "curious for"
wrong.text: He is curious for the answer.

meaning: Happy and sad at the same time.

examples.label: At home
examples.text: Moving out of my childhood home was **bittersweet**.

examples.label: With friends
examples.text: Our last day of college felt **bittersweet**.

right.label: ✓ For moments with joy and sadness

wrong.label: ✗ Not for a purely happy moment
wrong.text: Our holiday was perfect, totally bittersweet.
